name: @dszp/yealink-lib
description: Portable, Node-free toolkit for Yealink's device-management cloud (YMCS and RPS, one Open API): OAuth2 client-credentials auth with the timestamp/nonce headers, split read/write API clients, and skip/limit/autoCount pagination. Runs unchanged in a Cloudflare Worker, Node, or the browser.
//publishConfig: No `provenance: true` here on purpose: it would force provenance on EVERY publish, including the manual first one that a brand-new package requires (npm can only configure trusted publishing on a package that already exists). Provenance comes from the workflow's explicit `npm publish --provenance` in CI.

..//require: ESM-only package. This `require` condition lets Node >=22.12 load it via require(esm); older Node still gets an accurate ERR_REQUIRE_ESM here instead of the confusing ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED the bare export map produced.

//files: The maps and `src` ship together on purpose. tsc writes a sourceMappingURL pointer into every dist file, and the .d.ts.map references ../src/*.ts — so publishing the pointers WITHOUT them gave consumers a 404 and no Go-to-Definition: the cost of the flags with none of the benefit. With these, a Worker stack trace names a real .ts line and Go-to-Definition opens actual source. Same shape in all the @dszp/*-lib packages — change all of them or none.
//files-tests: src ships so the .d.ts.map references resolve and Go-to-Definition opens real source. The TESTS are not part of that: nothing in dist references them, they roughly double the tarball, and a stray comment in one of them is a leak with the same reach as a doc comment. Excluded by negation rather than by moving them, so they stay beside the code they test.

scripts.//prepublishOnly: Publish-only build with sourcemaps OFF. A normal `pnpm build` keeps maps for link: consumers.
